title: Planetary Nebula NGC 2371
caption: The planetary nebula NGC 2371, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
credit: NASA, ESA, and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the ESA/Hubble image archive. No published rating.

story: Prominent pink clouds lie on opposite sides of a central star in this glowing bubble of gas, with many tiny pink dots also lined up across the star. This is NGC 2371 in Gemini, a planetary nebula made from the cast-off gas of a star much like the Sun.

The star at the center is the super-hot core of a former red giant, stripped of its outer layers, with a surface temperature of about 240,000 degrees Fahrenheit. Its ultraviolet light makes the nebula glow. The pink color shows the paired clouds are relatively cool and dense.

The small pink knots seem to mark gas thrown out in a specific direction, and that direction has shifted over the past few thousand years. The reason is not well understood, though a second star orbiting the central one might be responsible. Within a few thousand years the nebula will fade away, and the star will cool into a white dwarf.

understand.summary: Hubble's Wide Field Planetary Camera 2 made this false-color image. Filters for sulfur and nitrogen are shown in red, hydrogen in green and oxygen in blue.
understand.eye: It is a false-color image in which each gas is assigned its own color, so it does not show what an eye would see.

explore: NGC 2371 lies about 4,300 light-years away. The images were taken with Wide Field Planetary Camera 2 as part of the Hubble Heritage program, and they revealed many structures not seen before.
alt: A glowing bubble of gas with pink clouds on opposite sides of a central star and a line of small pink knots.
